normalized_findings: Agents are persistent stateful environments powered by Durable Objects.
Repository documents state, SQLite, WebSockets, scheduling, model calls, MCP, Workflows, subagents, sandboxed execution and observability.
The agent requires a Durable Object binding and SQLite migration in Wrangler configuration.
Repository says the SDK is evolving quickly and is not accepting external pull requests.
evidence_limitations: Repository feature descriptions require independent runtime conformance testing.

normalized_findings: The current public agents package release is 0.17.4.
Release notes show active changes to MCP elicitation and hibernation recovery behavior.
evidence_limitations: A 0.x version and rapid release activity indicate API change risk; no general stability guarantee was found.

normalized_findings: Each Cloudflare-hosted agent session is documented with durable identity, local SQL storage, real-time connections, scheduled work and recoverable execution.
Deployment is explicitly coupled to Cloudflare's global network.
evidence_limitations: Mutable vendor documentation; hosting, durability and scale claims are not independent guarantees.

normalized_findings: Agents emit structured diagnostic events for RPC, state, schedules, workflows, MCP, lifecycle and chat recovery.
Workflow diagnostics include start, event, approval, rejection, termination, pause, resume and restart.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation; diagnostic events are implementation-specific and do not match AI LAB's normalized vocabulary one-for-one.

normalized_findings: Documented patterns include MCP elicitation, durable Workflow approval and Code Mode tool approval.
Workflow approvals can wait for months or longer without keeping an Agent running.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation; vendor approval primitives are not AI LAB authorization decisions.

normalized_findings: Workflows documents durable multi-step execution, persisted state, retries, external-event waits, approvals, pause, resume and termination.
Built-in observability and debugging are documented.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation; exact-once side effects are not promised.

normalized_findings: Each step is individually retryable and may persist state for continuation after failure.
Documentation tells developers to make side-effecting steps idempotent because steps can retry.
Batch instance creation is documented as idempotent for retained IDs, unlike the general create call.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation; application side-effect idempotency remains the developer's responsibility.

normalized_findings: Published limits cover CPU per step, persisted state, steps, retries, concurrency, creation rate and completed-state retention.
Waiting instances do not count toward active instance concurrency.
evidence_limitations: Mutable plan-dependent limits must be rechecked before any sandbox proposal.

normalized_findings: Pricing dimensions are CPU time, requests, persisted storage and executed steps.
Step and storage billing is announced to start no earlier than 2026-08-10.
Idle and waiting time does not incur CPU time.
evidence_limitations: Mutable forward-looking pricing; rates and billing start require review before use.

normalized_findings: Durable Objects provide globally unique identity, single-threaded coordination and private transactional strongly consistent storage per object.
Alarms wake an object for future work.
Storage is documented up to 10 GB per object.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation; consistency is per object, not global distributed database consistency.

normalized_findings: Jurisdiction restrictions are documented for EU, US and FedRAMP-Moderate locations.
Durable Object IDs may be logged outside the jurisdiction for billing and debugging.
Jurisdiction controls object compute and persistence but not request-response regions.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation; legal and privacy review is required for identifiers logged outside the selected jurisdiction.

normalized_findings: Durable Objects billing surfaces include requests, compute duration and storage operations/bytes.
WebSocket hibernation avoids duration billing while eligible and idle.
evidence_limitations: Mutable plan-dependent pricing and metering require exact reconciliation design.

normalized_findings: Workers AI is a model inference service and is not an agent runtime.
Pricing is published in per-model units and neurons; the catalog changes over time.
JSON Mode supports schema-requested structured output for selected models but does not guarantee schema satisfaction.
Cloudflare says Workers AI customer content is not used to train models or improve services without explicit consent; storage occurs when a storage product is deliberately combined with Workers AI.
evidence_limitations: Mutable documentation bundle normalized from overview, pricing, JSON Mode, data-usage and changelog pages; per-model behavior and terms require separate review.

findings.claim: Agents SDK 0.17.4 implements stateful agent identities as Durable Objects with SQLite state and WebSockets.
Durable Objects provide persistent per-object state and Workflows provide retryable persisted steps and external-event waits.
limitations: Cross-component failure and recovery semantics are not yet tested.

findings.claim: Workflow approval and MCP elicitation patterns support human pauses.
limitations: Not equivalent to AI LAB authorization.

findings.claim: Structured diagnostics and built-in Workflow observability are documented.
limitations: No exact AI LAB event-equivalence guarantee.

findings.claim: Public metering surfaces cover requests, CPU/duration, steps and storage.
limitations: Exact per-run reconciliation and upcoming billing change remain unresolved.

findings.claim: Workers AI is an inference component and must not be modeled as an agent runtime.
limitations: It may be bound as a separately governed inference candidate only.

findings.claim: The 0.x package and repository's evolving-quickly statement indicate material API change risk.

event_mapping.limitation: Connection is not necessarily session creation.
Tool event equivalence requires implementation inspection.
Tool event equivalence requires implementation inspection.
Several primitives implement different pause semantics.
MCP OAuth is not AI LAB authorization.
No stable generic start event was established.
No stable generic completion event was established.
No runtime-wide structured-result event guarantee was established.
Billing analytics are separate from a normalized per-step event.
Workflow steps do not cover every Agent step.
Workflow pause is not equivalent to every agent session wait.
No universal recursive agent-turn cancellation semantic was established.

portability_findings: Agents depend on Durable Objects, Wrangler bindings and Cloudflare deployment; runtime portability is low without a separate adapter/reimplementation.
Workers AI model/provider integration is separable from Agents runtime identity and must be governed independently.
privacy_findings: Public evidence does not establish chain-of-thought access or retention behavior for Agents; it remains unknown.
AI LAB adapters must not persist private model reasoning or chain-of-thought.
Durable Object jurisdiction controls have scope limitations and identifiers may be logged outside the selected jurisdiction.
Workers AI data-use claims apply to its inference service and do not automatically cover every external model provider used through Agents.
durability_findings: Strong per-object storage and retryable persisted Workflow steps provide credible durability primitives.
Ordering, idempotency, cancellation, replay and recovery across Agents, Workflows and external tools require conformance tests.
human_review_findings: Workflow approvals and MCP elicitation are documented.
AI LAB authorization remains a separate control-plane decision and cannot be delegated to vendor primitives.
sandbox_findings: The repository documents isolated Worker/virtual-filesystem execution as a feature.
Isolation, network egress, resource limits and persistence require independent security testing.
observability_findings: Structured diagnostic events exist for multiple components.
The common AI-120 event vocabulary cannot be inferred wholesale; many mappings remain undocumented or implementation-specific.
cost_accounting_findings: Workflows and Durable Objects publish metering units.
Exact Agent-session attribution across Workers, Durable Objects, Workflows, storage, inference and external providers is incomplete.
Workflows step/storage billing change is scheduled no earlier than 2026-08-10 and requires re-review.
unresolved_questions: What package API stability commitment applies to Agents 0.x?
What generic turn, action, result, cancellation and usage events are stable and exportable?
What chain-of-thought and reasoning retention behavior applies across model providers?
How are all component costs attributed and reconciled to one AI LAB run?
What sandbox egress and isolation guarantees are contractual?
How do instance restart, duplicate delivery and external side effects behave under failure?

historical_evidence_classification.reason: Repository snapshot of a prior direct Cloudflare infrastructure design; not current Agents SDK evidence.
The plan is explicitly retired as of 2026-07-13 and preserved only for lineage.
The deployment guide is explicitly retired and cannot authorize or prove a current runtime.
Local mocked implementation proves repository behavior only, not current Cloudflare platform guarantees.
